snip.t: Peripartum cardiomyopathy characterized by LV systolic dysfunction during the last trimester or early puerperium period.
Systemic and tropical risk factors: Recent delivery (peripartum cardiomyopathy, typically within 5 months postpartum); heavy alcohol intake; chemotherapy exposure (e.g., doxorubicin).
Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) presenting with acute decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
Cardiogenic: Primary pump failure — Rheumatic heart disease, acute coronary syndromes, endomyocardial fibrosis, peripartum cardiomyopathy
Peripartum cardiomyopathy → last month of pregnancy or 5 months postpartum
